source_text: Ille ergo dicit a principe tenebrarum, id est auctore mali, de duarum commixtione naturarum, bonae et malae, hominem creatum fuisse. Tu quid dicis? A Deo quidem bono, sed omnes homines malos creari.
pass_a_gloss: He therefore says that by the prince of darkness, that is the author of evil, from the mixture of two natures, good and evil, a human was created. You what do you say? By the good God indeed, but that all humans are created evils.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS creo; Blaise of God as maker

pass_b_english: He says, then, that the prince of darkness, the author of evil, created humanity by mixing two natures, good and evil. What do you say? That the good God indeed creates human beings, but creates them all evil.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
